findings.claim: ordinary hosts bit-identical; charge can only shrink
findings.evidence: View = min(physical, finite cgroup limit) <= physical always, so the 5% charge never increases: no previously-admitting configuration can newly refuse. limit is None on hosts without a finite limit (_container_memory_limit_bytes skips 'max' and >= 1<<60 sentinels - read and confirmed), and limits >= physical are ignored by the 0 < limit < view test. Verified live on this host: physical 376.05 GiB, cgroup limit 64.0 GiB, headroom 5.31 GiB; new default 3.200 GiB == 5% of min view; old formula 18.802 GiB; budget 2.653 GiB; census-config algebra 5% of 6 GiB = 322122547 exact.

findings.evidence: Read the call path: runtime._child_environment imports default_gdal_cache_bytes at call time (runtime.py:680 area) and sets GDAL_CACHEMAX from it; the charge side (_resolved_gdal_cache) calls the same function when unset. Residual point-in-time caveat (probes at two moments) is pre-existing and disclosed in the evidence doc.

findings.claim: default still refuses on this host, headroom-driven
findings.evidence: Reproduced the numbers: charge 3.200 GiB > budget 2.653 GiB here because the budget uses cgroup HEADROOM (limit - usage) while the charge uses the limit. This asymmetry is intentional (budget must stay headroom-correct); the evidence doc says so explicitly. The s03b doc's '68.7 GB cgroup' equals the measured 64.0 GiB (GB vs GiB) - consistent.

findings.claim: python-float Tgwall ~1 ulp apart from the ndarray set on 5/6 Lcyl fields
findings.evidence: Claim verified by independent execution, with one nuance the doc omits: the partition is DTYPE-CONDITIONAL. With f64 Tgwall wrappers I measure 1-2 ulp divergence on exactly 5/6 fields (Lsouth 0 ulp; 3 seeds); with f32 wrappers python-float is bit-IDENTICAL to the ndarray set (0 ulp, 3 seeds) - the coefficient arithmetic stays f32 either way (engine._operands leaves f32 + weak python float at f32; any ndarray wrapper promotes to f64 only when the wrapper is f64). The doc states the partition unconditionally. Direction is conservative (it under-claims bit-equality), so no risk to the contract, but the dtype condition should be recorded.
Comment cites 'patch_radiation._is_singleton; T01 admission' - no such function exists; the helper is _uniform_tgwall. Comment drift only.
